title: Measures to Mitigate Increasing Cost of Living
what_it_is: Measures to Mitigate Increasing Cost of Living

sections.label: Cost of living and measures
sections.summary: A question asks whether the cost of living has risen significantly and what measures the Government will take to address further cost increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the general cost of living in Singapore has increased significantly and is a cause for concern; and (b) what are the measures that the Government will take to address further cost increases and minimise their impact on the low- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There are absolute measures of how the prices of a particular basket of goods and services change over time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There can also be relative and evolving interpretations of what constitutes an essential basket of goods and services for different groups of Singaporeans.

sections.label: No single cost measure
sections.summary: No single measure fully expresses an individual's cost of living pressures given different needs, wants and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As such, no single measure will express an individual's "cost of living" pressures fully, given the different needs and wants, the evolving aspirations and the potential gap between aspirations and anticipated means.

sections.label: Bunched price increases and CPI
sections.summary: Bunched price increases can have a disproportionate psychological impact; last year CPI-All Items inflation was +0.6%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The "bunching" of price increases, like the increases in water and electricity prices this month, can also have a disproportionate psychological impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Last year, the Consumer Price Index (CPI)-All Items inflation was +0.6%, lower than the average of +2.3% between 2007 and 2017.

sections.label: 2017 inflation by income group
sections.summary: 2017 inflation was -0.1% for the lowest 20%, +0.5% for the middle 60% and +0.8% for the top 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The 2017 inflation figures for the various household income groups with their respective baskets of goods and services were -0.1% for the lowest 20%, +0.5% for the middle 60%, and +0.8% for the top 20%.

sections.label: Inflation excluding imputed rental
sections.summary: Stripping out imputed rental for owner-occupied accommodation shows retiree household inflation was +2.1% last year, higher than other groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: However, I asked them to strip out the imputed rental for owner-occupied accommodation from the CPI, because this will give an indication of the inflationary pressures that they might feel from the cash outlay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And inflation for retiree households was +2.1% last year, higher than the other household income groups.

sections.label: Expected CPI inflation range
sections.summary: CPI-All Items inflation is expected to remain low this year, between +0.5% and 1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: CPI-All Items inflation is expected to remain low this year, between +0.5% and 1%.

sections.label: Open Electricity Market soft launch
sections.summary: EMA began a soft launch of the Open Electricity Market in Jurong, giving 108,000 households and 9,500 small businesses retailer options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In April this year, EMA commenced the soft launch of the Open Electricity Market in Jurong, allowing 108,000 households and 9,500 small businesses the option to buy electricity from a retailer with a price plan that best meets their needs.

sections.label: New hawker centres with affordable food
sections.summary: NEA announced 20 new hawker centres with about 800 stalls to be built by 2027, with managing agents required to provide affordable food options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) has also announced that 20 new hawker centres with approximately 800 stalls will be built by 2027 and the managing agents appointed to run these new centres, some of which are social enterprises, will also be required to provide affordable food options in each of these hawker centres.

sections.label: GST Voucher U-Save rebate increase
sections.summary: Budget 2017 announced a permanent increase to the GST Voucher U-Save rebate to offset utility bill increases after water price revisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In Budget 2017, the Government announced a permanent increase to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher U-Save rebate to offset some of the increases in utility bills for the lower- and lower middle-income households following the water price revisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With the additional U-Save rebates, 1- and 2-room HDB households, including most 3-roomers, will not see an increase in overall water bills on average.

sections.label: Price transparency for household items
sections.summary: The Government will work with NTUC and CASE on price transparency platforms and a stakeholder panel to oversee the effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: One way is to improve price transparency on common household items like groceries and cooked food so that consumers can be more informed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will work with NTUC and CASE to see how best to bring about such platforms for our consumers, tapping on the local networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will also work with NTUC and CASE to establish a panel comprising relevant stakeholders, such as merchants’ associations, unions and grassroots leaders, to help oversee this effort and look into ground feedback to help consumers stretch their hard-earned dollar, while deterring unfair pricing of consumer necessities.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice affordable products expansion
sections.summary: NTUC FairPrice will expand its House Brand range and more FairPrice Shop stores will be set up to make affordable products accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: NTUC FairPrice continues to expand its House Brand product range of affordable value-for-money alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will work with NTUC to establish more NTUC FairPrice Shop stores in our neighbourhoods to make affordable products more accessible to all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: By helping to moderate the prices of essential goods and services, social enterprises, such as NTUC, play an important role in benchmarking prices across the board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: One in yellow for the senior citizens, one in pink for families with school-going children, and one in blue for young couples.

sections.label: Support for those most in need
sections.summary: The Government is committed to helping Singaporeans stretch their hard-earned dollar, with support first given to those most in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Beyond creating opportunities for Singaporeans to enjoy real wage growth to meet their aspirations, the Government is also committed to helping Singaporeans stretch their hard-earned dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At the same time, we are also cognisant that, with finite resources, support must, first and foremost, be given to those most in need.

sections.label: Help for middle-income group
sections.summary: The Member asks what more the Government can do to help the sandwich middle-income group cope with cost of living increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While I appreciate the efforts that are targeted primarily at our low-income Singaporeans to cope with the increase in cost of living, I would like to ask the Minister what more can the Government do to help the sandwich middle-income group.

sections.label: Government concern across family spectrum
sections.summary: The Government is concerned not just with lower-income, so MTI and agencies were asked to look across all families, including retirees and middle-income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government is concerned not just with the lower-income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is the reason why I have asked the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and the various agencies to look across the entire spectrum of families in Singapore – retirees, middle-income group – because they all face different pressures.

sections.label: Decile bands and worker transition
sections.summary: Staff were asked to look at each decile band, with attention to workers facing lower or stagnating wage increases, working with MOM and NTUC on transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And I would like to add one more point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have personally asked my staff to look at each of the decile band because, while our averages are moving up, we are obviously conscious that not everyone will move up at the same pace or the same rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And we have to pay particular attention to the group that I mentioned just now who have lower wage increases or stagnating wage increases because their industries are going through rapid transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is where we will work closely with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and NTUC to help our workers transit to a new industry, to acquire new skills and take on new jobs before they are displaced.

sections.label: Help those who need more
sections.summary: With available resources, as a family or society, the most help must go to those who need it a bit more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Last, but not least, with the resources that we have, either as a family or as a society, we must make sure that we give the most help to those who need it a bit more than us.

sections.label: Coffee shop and NTUC food prices
sections.summary: Residents report coffee shop food price rises of 50 cents and say NTUC food prices are not necessarily the cheapest, urging the Minister to look into it.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The second question – I have residents who keep telling me that food prices in some of the coffee shops have gone up even before the effect of water price increase or electricity tariff increase.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Each increase is 50 cents – from $3.00 to $3.50, from $3.50 to $4.00, unlike previously, when the increase was 10 cents or 20 cents.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The third question – I also got feedback from residents, because in Nee Soon South, we have NTUC and we also have Sheng Siong.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I heard from residents that – giving due respect to our colleague Mr Seah Kian Peng and those who are in NTUC – the food or the price of those things sold in NTUC nowadays are not necessarily the cheapest.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I would like to urge the Minister to look into this.

sections.label: Food price increase rate falling
sections.summary: Food prices are still increasing but the rate has come down from 3.3% to 2.1% to 1.4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The one that the Member referred to, I think, is the second chart, right?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That means food prices are still increasing but the rate has come down from what used to be 3.3%, to 2.1% to 1.4%.

sections.label: Anti-Profiteering Committee decision
sections.summary: The speaker says he considered setting up an Anti-Profiteering Committee and proposes a different approach under strategy No 7.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second thing, whether we will set up the Anti-Profiteering Committee, I have thought long and hard about this and we have previous experiences on how to be more effective, which is why for strategy No 7, I have proposed to do things a bit differently to give us better and faster results.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice item monitoring
sections.summary: NTUC FairPrice monitors 500 items daily and ensures they average 4%-5% below the whole basket of goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And NTUC FairPrice monitors the 500 items every day – their own 500 items and what the market is selling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: They will make sure that, on average, their 500 items will be 4%-5% below the whole basket of goods.

sections.label: NTUC role in services
sections.summary: NTUC works with Ministries in eldercare and early childhood education to understand benchmarks, giving the market a pricing anchor point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, NTUC in the sector of eldercare, early childhood education also performs the same role, which is that they help and work with the Ministries to understand the benchmark and the drivers for those services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And because of that, the entire market has an anchor point, if you like, in their pricing strategy and will not be carried away with just price competition.

sections.label: Global interest rate hike impacts
sections.summary: Interest rate hikes have direct cost, exchange rate and global business confidence impacts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Likewise, for any interest rate hikes across the global markets, there is the direct and indirect impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The direct impact is that it adds to the cost of doing business and the second impact is that it will affect the relative exchange rate, which will then affect the strength of the Singapore dollar to contain imported inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But the most important third-level impact of any interest rate hike across the world is the impact on global business confidence.

sections.label: Consumer choice and business costs
sections.summary: The speaker cites consumer choice and extends the open electricity market, while monitoring rents for spikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So long as we have a variety of choices for our consumers, we let them choose within their means to see what best suits their family needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We agree with Mr Seah Kian Peng's second point that utilities, rents and labour will be concerns for businesses, which is why we are extending the open electricity market to more consumers and small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For rents, as I have mentioned, we will closely monitor the trend to make sure that their rents do not spike because of insufficient space for our businesses to do their business.

sections.label: CASE and MTI transparency
sections.summary: CASE would work with MTI to provide better transparency so consumers know which businesses offer best value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: CASE would be happy to work with MTI to try to provide better transparency so that consumers would be able to know which businesses provide the best value to consumers.

sections.label: Lease length commercial decision
sections.summary: The speaker says lease length cannot be mandated because it is a commercial decision between the renting entity and the taker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, on the issue of the leases, I think we cannot mandate the length of the leases because it is a commercial decision between the commercial entity renting out the place and the one taking it up.

sections.label: Anti-competitive behaviour MTI action
sections.summary: The speaker reassures Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that MTI and the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore will take up anti-competitive behaviour issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the other issue, I would just like to reassure Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that when there are issues that have to deal with anti-competitive behaviour, then MTI, together with the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore, will make sure we take these up.

sections.label: CPI by demographic groups
sections.summary: The question asks whether MTI would consider measuring and publishing the CPI based on different demographic groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would MTI consider measuring and publishing the CPI based on different demographic groups?
